AgentCatalog.description: What THIS deploy can run; `doors` gates the tools.

doors.description: Each tool's door status BEFORE a run, keyed by AgentTool (web_search, find_contacts): 'open' gates the toggle on; any other code is the reason it is off (today only 'not_configured' can appear here; the run-time codes ride the cells).
doors.title: Doors

search_provider.description: Which door serves web search on this deployment (the server's SearchProvider, pinned by a parity test), or null where none is configured. Client copy composes it: a rate-limited cell names the paid door only where it is a remedy, never to someone already on it.
search_provider.title: Search Provider

support_followup.description: The deployment's needs-attention follow-up, profile-owned server-side (check the logs locally; the operator's support channel hosted). Client copy composes it instead of hedging about an operator it cannot identify.
support_followup.title: Support Followup

truncated.description: True when the catalog cap cut the list: an address past the cap may still RUN (model_for validates against the full roster), it just is not shown.
truncated.title: Truncated

AgentCatalog.title: AgentCatalog

AgentConfig.description:
The runtime's interchange unit, shared by both custodies (a
saved agent, a column's quick prompt) and the test bench.

source.description: Which server of that spec (the env-named source).
source.title: Source

AgentConfig.title: AgentConfig

AgentListItem.description:
One list row: the index ships what the table renders, never
each agent's whole config (a full list of maxed prompts would be
megabytes to draw four columns; the edit page fetches its agent by
id).
AgentListItem.title: AgentListItem

AgentOutput.description:
One declared output: a named, described field the model must
fill (the description rides into the instruction), landing as one
cell per row.

key.description: Present always; BLANK allowed on requests (the server derives it from the label) and always populated on responses (required, no default: a response omitting it must fail the parse, never invent an empty string).
key.title: Key

label.description: Non-blank on the wire (the server refuses blank labels at the request boundary); the builder's local draft may hold blank rows, client-side only.
label.title: Label

type.description: Sheet display type; drives rendering only.
type.title: Type

AgentOutput.title: AgentOutput

AgentSummary.description: A stored agent (one custody of a config).

ephemeral.description: True for a column-owned quick-prompt agent: hidden from the roster, excluded from MAX_AGENTS, deleted with its column.
ephemeral.title: Ephemeral

AgentSummary.title: AgentSummary

AgentTestResult.description:
One hand-fed row's outcome: the cells it would write (possibly
empty, honestly), the evidence the model saw, and the searches that
produced it with each query's diagnosis.
AgentTestResult.title: AgentTestResult

AgentTestRun.description:
The polled test-run envelope: result rides only when complete,
and a failed run carries its WHY (every empty result ships its
diagnosis; failure is the tier that needs it most).

poll_budget_seconds.description: The runtime's own worst case for one run: a poller waits this long (plus its margin) and no longer. The server presents runs still pending past its LARGER stale window as failed, so the loop normally ends on a terminal status.
poll_budget_seconds.title: Poll Budget Seconds

AgentTestRun.title: AgentTestRun

AgentTools.description:
The tool REGISTRY, one typed field per tool: the wire itself
carries the key set, so the web derives its tool list from this
shape instead of hand-retyping it. Unknown keys are TOLERATED
(dropped) here because this model validates on every read, and a
server that adds a tool must not fail stored rows or a browser
holding the old bundle; the REQUEST leg's serializer is where
unknown keys refuse, which is what keeps the set closed on the
way in.
AgentTools.title: AgentTools

AuthUser.description:
The authenticated user the app's /v1/auth/me returns (and the identity
the IdP resolves). Char-pointer ULIDs, so plain strings on the wire.
AuthUser.title: AuthUser

CatalogModel.description: One runnable model on this deploy.
CatalogModel.title: CatalogModel

CellStateWire.description:
One AI cell's state and the tool statuses of the run that wrote
it: `tools` is tool -> status code (a base ToolStatus code or the
tool's own; "open" for a tool that served), empty for a pending
cell or a run before tools reported statuses. The client resolves
copy by (tool, code) and tolerates a code it has not heard of.
CellStateWire.title: CellStateWire

ColumnFill.description:
A column's fill linkage: present exactly on AI columns (the
agent that fills it; the ephemeral-vs-roster custody rides the
agent, not the column).

current_fill_id.description: The fill run that speaks for this column, stored here when it opens. Blank on a column filled before it was recorded. Clients read it off ColumnFillSummary, which the fills poll serves; it is declared here because this model is what the column's own structure is, and an undeclared key is dropped on every list read.
current_fill_id.title: Current Fill Id

ColumnFill.title: ColumnFill

ColumnFillSummary.description:
Per-column coverage, computed server-side so the client renders
instead of reconstructing (a client sum over one PAGE of fills
silently undercounts the moment history outgrows the page).

Deliberately NOT carrying how many rows a refill would target: that
is planning-grade math on a four-second progress poll. It is asked
once, on the consent path, where it has to be exact anyway.

attempted.description: Cells this column's fills have RESOLVED: filled plus diagnosed blanks. A targeted cell ends in exactly one of those two places, so their sum is what the column was asked to do. It is the honest denominator for filled; the sheet's row count is a different question.
attempted.title: Attempted

current_fill_id.description: The newest fill run naming this column; "" when none is exposed.
current_fill_id.title: Current Fill Id

current_status.description: The status of the run current_fill_id names; "" when the column has never run. The page's runs list is LIVE runs only, so this is where a terminal story lands.
current_status.title: Current Status

filled.description: Cells in this column that hold a value.
filled.title: Filled

last_error.description: The newest run's error, both legs (tier 1: the message renders verbatim); None unless that run FAILED, so a newer clean run clears it and a stopped run carries none.

ColumnFillSummary.title: ColumnFillSummary

ColumnPromptWire.description:
The column's CURRENT fill config as the server holds it (GET),
and the echo after a column-scoped edit (PATCH
/lists/{id}/columns/{key}/prompt). Live fills keep their frozen
snapshot; an edit reaches the NEXT fill's admission, so surfaces
peeking at "what fills this column" read HERE, never a fill's
snapshot.
ColumnPromptWire.title: ColumnPromptWire

Company.description:
One company from the central universe (seeded from the free PDL
Company Dataset, CC BY 4.0). Char-pointer ULID id.

id.description: The company's ULID in the universe.
id.title: Id

linkedin_url.description: LinkedIn company URL; empty when unknown.
linkedin_url.title: Linkedin Url

size_band.description: Coarse employee band, e.g. 1-10; empty when unknown.
size_band.title: Size Band

snapshot_date.description: ISO date the row's data was current.
snapshot_date.title: Snapshot Date

source.description: Provenance of the row, e.g. pdl_free.
source.title: Source

Company.title: Company

FillCounters.description:
Worker-written progress (never COUNT(*) polling): attempted is
rows with a terminal outcome this fill; blank counts diagnosed
blanks; transient counts rows currently parked in retry.
FillCounters.title: FillCounters

FillError.description:
A failed fill's two-tier why: `code` is the machine leg (client
branching), `message` is server-authored copy rendered verbatim.
FillError.title: FillError

FillRunPage.description:
LIVE runs plus the per-column summaries. Terminal runs do not
ride the poll: a finished run's story (its status, its error) lands
on the column summary the moment it leaves this list, so the page
carries the in-flight work and the summaries carry everything a
column needs to say about its past.

columns.description: One summary per AI column of the list this page belongs to.
columns.title: Columns

next_cursor.description: The last id when more runs exist.
next_cursor.title: Next Cursor

runs.description: LIVE runs only. Named for what it holds rather than the house `items`, because this page carries a second collection (`columns`) and `items` beside it would name neither.
runs.title: Runs

FillRunPage.title: FillRunPage

FillRunWire.description:
The fill run envelope. The POST and cancel ECHOES carry every
state (a failed run is an API object with its error, not a 4xx);
the fills LIST the sheet re-attaches to carries live runs only
(see FillRunPage).

column_keys.description: The columns this run owns, frozen at consent.
column_keys.title: Column Keys

confirmed_row_count.description: Rows this run TARGETED, fixed when it opened: the progress denominator. The consent echo is a REQUEST field of the same name that admission compares against the sheet, 409ing on drift; what ships here is what the walk actually consented to, which a scoped fill makes smaller than the sheet.
confirmed_row_count.title: Confirmed Row Count

error.description: This run's error, both legs (tier 1: the message renders verbatim); None unless the run FAILED, the same predicate ColumnFillSummary.last_error states.

heartbeat_at.description: Stamped with each counter write; the client judges staleness against ROW_LEASE_STALE_SECONDS off the wire, warning-role only (never presented as failure).
heartbeat_at.title: Heartbeat At

started_by.description: User id, ATTRIBUTION only; authorization is account membership.
started_by.title: Started By

FillRunWire.title: FillRunWire

FolderSummary.description: A flat, account-scoped bucket for lists (taxonomy, not behavior).

list_count.description: Server-side count; consent copy must not trust loaded pages.
list_count.title: List Count

FolderSummary.title: FolderSummary

skipped.description: Blank lines and rows wider than the header, not imported.
skipped.title: Skipped

key.description: Stable snake_case key; row data dicts key on it.
key.title: Key

label.description: Display label, as the user (or the CSV header) wrote it.
label.title: Label

type.description: Sheet display type; drives rendering only.
type.title: Type

data.description: Cell values keyed by column key.
data.title: Data

states.description: AI cell states keyed by column key: every cell without a value, plus filled cells whose run had a degraded tool. Slim on absences by contract, so a long-filled sheet carries almost nothing here. A value in `data` with no entry here IS filled and clean, and never-attempted is likewise an absence.
states.title: States

next_cursor.description: The last position when more rows exist.
next_cursor.title: Next Cursor

ListSummary.description: One list as the index shows it (and the save-list response).

folder_id.description: The containing folder; empty = loose at the root.
folder_id.title: Folder Id

origin.description: How the list came to exist.
origin.title: Origin

origin_ref.description: e.g. the source run id for discover snapshots.
origin_ref.title: Origin Ref

row_count.description: Total rows (the sheet may page far beyond one response).
row_count.title: Row Count

ListSummary.title: ListSummary

next_cursor.description: The last id when more lists exist.
next_cursor.title: Next Cursor

LookalikeGroup.description:
One seed group of a run: heterogeneous cohorts split into distinct
groups, each searched by its own centroid and labeled.

elbow_rank.description: This group's own boundary: the knee of ITS score decay (null when too short/flat).
elbow_rank.title: Elbow Rank

label.description: Human label; empty for the single homogeneous group.
label.title: Label

size.description: Results this group contributed to the run.
size.title: Size

LookalikeGroup.title: LookalikeGroup

description.description: Site-derived blurb (homepage meta description or title); empty until the domain has a fetched snippet.
description.title: Description

group.description: Label of the seed group that surfaced this candidate; empty for single-group runs.
group.title: Group

LookalikeListResponse.description:
The look-alike envelope (data service and app proxy alike), for both
the query POST and the run-status poll.

`status` drives the async lifecycle: "complete" carries the page in
`items`; "pending"/"running" mean poll the run (HTTP 202, empty items);
"failed" carries `detail`; "canceled" is terminal by request (a fresh
query revives the run). The engine computes in a worker, so a cold
cohort answers pending first and is polled by `run_id`; a cached cohort
answers complete inline.

detail.description: Failure detail when status is failed.
detail.title: Detail

engine.description: Which engine ranked these, e.g. embedding_v1.
engine.title: Engine

groups.description: The run's seed-group breakdown; single unlabeled entry for homogeneous cohorts.
groups.title: Groups

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page.
next_cursor.title: Next Cursor

outlier_domains.description: Seeds set aside by clustering as misfits (excluded from generation, shown to the user).
outlier_domains.title: Outlier Domains

result_count.description: TOTAL results in the completed run (the full lead-list size, independent of page size).
result_count.title: Result Count

run_id.description: The run to poll; null only when no run exists (e.g. an empty cohort).
run_id.title: Run Id

status.description: Run lifecycle. Terminal: complete | failed | canceled; keep polling: pending | running.
status.title: Status

unresolved_domains.description: Inline seed domains that are not in the universe.
unresolved_domains.title: Unresolved Domains

LookalikeListResponse.title: LookalikeListResponse

TestSearch.description:
One search query's outcome: `status` is what the door said (a
SearchStatus code: open, and hits, possibly zero, is the honest
answer; any other code is why there are none). `provider` is the
door that served it, `attempts` how many tries the seam made for
this one query (a rate limit is retried, same query, before it
counts), and `tool` which tool asked (web_search | find_contacts),
so a reader can tell whose door refused.
TestSearch.title: TestSearch
